question: Before the amalgamation of Dutch companies into the VOC in 1602, several independent voyages were organized by pre-companies (Voorcompagnieën). Which of the following statements is historically correct regarding these pre-VOC voyages?
options: The very first pre-company voyage in 1595 successfully established a permanent fort in Pulicat.
Between 1595 and 1601, fifteen fleets comprising 65 ships were dispatched to the East Indies by various pre-companies.
All pre-company voyages were financially backed by the Dutch State Treasury to compete with Spain.
The pre-companies strictly avoided the Coromandel coast and focused only on the Red Sea and Bengal.
explanation: In the 'wild years' of Dutch navigation (1595-1601), before the Dutch government forced an amalgamation, numerous rival companies called Voorcompagnieën (pre-companies) sent 15 fleets containing 65 ships to the East. This intense domestic competition drove up the purchase price of spices in Asia and drove down sale prices in Europe, which prompted the States-General to consolidate them into a single monopoly company (the VOC) in 1602.
